spec.rationale: A horse torso carried on matching horse legs keeps size and stride aligned for stable quadruped walking and running, while a donkey head provides a compatible herbivore muzzle and ears for grazing. This concept carries a flagged habitat conflict and climate conflict from non-overlapping horse and donkey ranges, functions as terrestrial in wetlands with low water dependence, and is crepuscular by design choice.
spec.name: Grey Ridge Courser

warnings.message: A fusion design inspired by a real hybrid must not claim the real hybrid's fertility unless its parents and cross direction match that hybrid exactly.
warnings.detail: documented real hybrid(s): hinny (father: horse (Equus caballus) × mother: donkey (Equus asinus); fertility fertile=no; Male horse (stallion) x female donkey (jenny); reciprocal cross to mule; most reports say hinnies are sterile); mule (father: donkey (Equus asinus) × mother: horse (Equus caballus); fertility fertile=no; Male donkey (jack) x female horse (mare); source classification E. africanus asinus male x E. ferus caballus female, mapped to pilot GBIF names Equus asinus and Equus caballus; odd chromosome number makes gamete formation difficult, often infertile, rare mare mule births reported). This fusion does not inherit their fertility.

warnings.message: A fusion's habitat list must overlap at least one habitat of each parent, or the non-overlap must be flagged as a habitat conflict.
warnings.detail: no shared habitat: horse forest/grassland/tundra/wetland; donkey desert/mountain

warnings.message: A fusion's climate list must overlap at least one climate of each parent, or the non-overlap must be flagged as a climate conflict.
warnings.detail: no shared climate: horse polar/temperate; donkey arid

warnings.message: A fusion with no habitat overlap with a parent must be flagged as a habitat conflict in the test output.
warnings.detail: no shared habitat: horse forest/grassland/tundra/wetland; donkey desert/mountain

warnings.message: A fusion with a wetland parent must not be recorded as purely terrestrial or purely aquatic without a note on its water dependence.
A fusion recorded in a wetland must state whether it is aquatic, semi-aquatic or terrestrial in that wetland.

A fusion combining a diurnal parent with a nocturnal parent must state its active_time as the overlap or as a design choice with a note; it may not be recorded as both fully diurnal and fully nocturnal.
warnings.detail: horse is crepuscular; donkey is diurnal/nocturnal

spec.prompt:
Reference image 1 shows a horse. Use it only for the torso, limbs and tail.
Reference image 2 shows a donkey. Use it only for the head and skin covering.
Create one new creature with a single, committed quadruped body plan.
Place the horse's torso, limbs and tail on the donkey's frame so every join heals naturally: no visible seams, no floating parts, no duplicated limbs.
Stay close to the documented hinny, a real hybrid of these parents. no shared habitat: horse forest/grassland/tundra/wetland; donkey desert/mountain no shared climate: horse polar/temperate; donkey arid no shared habitat: horse forest/grassland/tundra/wetland; donkey desert/mountain
Show the full body in a calm three-quarter view on a plain, softly lit background, in the style of a natural history field-guide plate. Photographic realism, accurate anatomy, no text, no labels, no people.
